SharedFlowBundle.name: SF-Signature-Validator
SharedFlowBundle.Description: Single entry point for signature validation at the gateway (the API itself provides no validation method). Calling API proxies set the signature.verify.type flow variable (jwt | cavage | xmldsig) and invoke this shared flow via FlowCallout; it routes to the matching sub-step. JWT/JWS is fully native (VerifyJWS, no JS at all): the verification public key (PEM) and KnownHeaders both resolve per-proxy from the shared KVM "signature" via ref, with KnownHeaders/IgnoreCriticalHeaders enforcing RFC 7515 §4.1.11's "crit" rule. The public key is stored as PEM directly in KVM rather than read from the KeyStore at request time: VerifyJWS's own does not resolve a dynamic ref at runtime (confirmed against a live Apigee instance; only ServiceCallout/TargetEndpoint's SSLInfo does that), and there's no Java-callout SDK method to reach KeyStore key material either — the only documented way (the Management API's cert-export endpoint) is an antipattern to call from a running proxy per Apigee's own docs, so the PEM is populated once, out-of-band, whenever the certificate is issued/rotated (see EV-JWT-Verify-Parse-Config). Cavage verifies everything achievable without real RSA/ECDSA math (the signing string) natively in JS, and faults via a clearly marked NI-Cavage-Verify-Signature placeholder for the actual cryptographic check, which needs a JavaCallout — Apigee has no native policy for raw-string signature verification, and JS can't reach KeyStore key material to do that math itself. XML-DSig verification IS fully implemented: one JavaCallout (JC-XmlDsig-Verify-Signature) does canonicalization, digest, and the SignatureValue check together, using the JDK's built-in JSR 105 implementation (javax.xml.crypto.dsig — no extra library beyond the Apigee SDK). Its verification public key is PEM-in-KVM too, same pattern and reason as JWT.
